name: Sprocket
text: Do weekly automated scans of all prompts using exact string matching to flag duplicates. This catches exact copies faster than semantic scans, cutting noise in reviews. Trade-off: misses near-duplicates that rephrase the same idea.

name: Gauge
text: Exact string matching fails when prompts change slightly—like adding a comma or a space. A light semantic scan still risks false positives—two prompts may embed similar ideas but serve different purposes. Use a hybrid approach: first run exact matching to catch obvious duplicates, then apply a lightweight semantic scan to catch near-duplicates, and manually review edge cases. Settle it by testing both methods on a sample of prompts and measuring false positives and false negatives.

name: Gauge
text: Light semantic scans still risk false positives—two prompts may embed similar ideas but serve different intents, wasting review time. A better alternative: run exact matching first, then only flag semantic matches that share at least one unique keyword tied to the prompt’s core function. Settle it by testing both methods on a 100-prompt sample and measuring false positives vs. missed near-duplicates.

name: Ratchet
text: DECISION: Run weekly hybrid scans—exact string matching first to catch trivial duplicates, then keyword-tied semantic scans to flag near-duplicates only when they share a core function keyword. Result: a single automated script that outputs a clean list of duplicates (exact and near) with review-ready notes. Owner: Sprocket.
